title: Convert route targets to bucket editor
summary: Replace the Settings TV/Movie route target table with a compact bucket editor and derived height-range rail while preserving existing control IDs and backend-owned behavior.
reason: The route target settings are three editable buckets, not a large data set. A bucket editor makes the derived ranges and per-bucket controls easier to scan than a wide five-column table.
behavior_before: The Settings route target section presented three route buckets as a wide editable table with repeated column headers and weaker emphasis on the derived height ranges.
behavior_after: The Settings route target section presents a horizontal height-range rail followed by three bucket cards that group encoded target size, direct-copy limits, height tolerance, and derived range for each bucket.

rollback_plan: Revert the Settings partial, Settings page CSS, and focused static test changes for the route target bucket editor, refresh generated summaries, and rerun targeted WebView settings tests.
notes:
Presentation-only WebView change. Existing input/output IDs remain intact; backend Preview/Save remains authoritative. No media policy, settings persistence, queue, pending-publish, rename, source/scratch/output movement, cleanup, or filesystem mutation behavior is changed.
Converted the Settings route targets from the wide table to a derived range rail and three bucket editor cards while preserving existing control IDs.
Refreshed generated summaries for the route target bucket editor change.
